summary.text: A Mars rover is a remote-controlled motor vehicle designed to travel on the surface of Mars.
Rovers examine more territory than stationary landers and can be directed to interesting features.
As of May 2021, six robotic rovers had succeeded on Mars: five managed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Zhurong, managed by China's space agency.

facts.label: Curiosity
facts.value: Landed in Gale Crater on August 6, 2012

facts.label: Zhurong
facts.value: First non-American rover to operate on Mars

items.prompt: A scientist spots an interesting feature far from where the craft touched down. Why does a rover help?

options.label: It can circle overhead and photograph the feature
It can be directed to the feature and cover more territory
It stays tethered to a base so it never gets lost
It can stay put and wait for the feature to come near

items.explain: Rovers examine more territory than stationary landers and can be directed to interesting features.

items.prompt: Dark, cold months are approaching on Mars. What can a rover do about it that a fixed lander cannot?

options.label: Place itself in a sunny position
Fly above the clouds until spring
Dig a shelter and switch itself off
Send the winter weather data to Earth first

items.explain: Unlike stationary landers, rovers can place themselves in sunny positions to weather winter months.

items.prompt: Which rover relied on the Mars Pathfinder base station to talk to Earth, rather than working on its own?

options.label: Sojourner
Spirit
Opportunity
Curiosity

items.explain: Sojourner depended on the Mars Pathfinder base station for communication, while Opportunity, Spirit and Curiosity were on their own.

items.prompt: Opportunity sent its last status after something stopped it from recharging its batteries. What was it?

options.label: Its wheels became trapped in sand
The Pathfinder base station went silent
A global dust storm blocked the sunlight
It ran past its planned mission length

items.explain: A global Mars dust storm blocked the sunlight needed to recharge its batteries. Trapped wheels were Spirit's problem.

items.prompt: Zhurong was switched off ahead of sandstorms and Martian winter. Why did it never restart by itself?

options.label: Its batteries had been removed to save weight
Its landing site was buried under a sandstorm
Its camera had been dropped on the ground
More dust than expected covered its solar panels

items.explain: A larger-than-expected build-up of dust covering its solar panels prevented it from self-reactivation.

items.prompt: Perseverance is NASA's rover built on the design of an earlier success. Which one?

options.label: Curiosity
Sojourner
Spirit
Opportunity

items.explain: Perseverance is NASA's rover based on the successful Curiosity design.
